# Numerous.ai Pricing: Is It Worth Your Money in 2026?


By


Drew Hahn · 13 min read


[X](https://x.com/JuliusAI)[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/julius-ai/)


You've got a thousand rows in a spreadsheet and a ChatGPT tab open in the next window, pasting one cell in and one answer back out, over and over. Numerous.ai exists to kill that exact workflow.


Numerous.ai pricing runs from $8 to $24 a month on yearly billing, plus a per-seat Enterprise tier for teams. I went through every plan to see where your money goes and whether it's worth paying for in 2026.


## Numerous.ai pricing: at a glance


Numerous.ai keeps it simple with three plans, though you won't see any of these numbers until you're a few steps into signing up.

## Numerous.ai pricing plans breakdown


I've tested a handful of AI spreadsheet tools,


and Numerous.ai keeps its pricing simpler than most:


### Personal plan: $19/month, or $8/month billed annually


-


What's included:


1 million characters of ChatGPT input and output, use in both Google Sheets and Excel, single user.


-


Best for:


Solo users who want AI in a few cells without wiring up an API key.


-


Pros:


The price gets you into Google Sheets and Excel both, so you're not locked to one app.


-


Cons:


That 1 million characters number counts your prompt and the answer together. A meaty prompt plus a paragraph reply can burn a few thousand characters each, so heavy users get through it faster than they expect. If your work leans on


[AI formulas in Google Sheets](https://julius.ai/articles/google-sheets-ai-formula) , watch this number.


### Pro plan: $39/month, or $24/month billed annually


-


What's included:


5 million characters, sharing with up to three people, and email support.


-


Best for:


Freelancers and small teams categorizing lists, cleaning data, or generating content across hundreds of rows.


-


Pros:


The jump from 1 million to 5 million characters gives real headroom for bulk jobs, plus you can loop in two teammates at no extra cost.


-


Cons:


Email support is the only service upgrade over Personal. If you need faster response times, this plan won't get you there.


### Enterprise plan: $10/user/month, or $8/user/month billed annually (3-seat minimum)


-


What's included:


1 million characters per user, priority email support, and a video onboarding call if you ask for one.


-


Best for:


Teams that want everyone standardized on the same plan with a single bill.


-


Pros:


Priority support and optional onboarding calls can save setup time for teams rolling this out across a department.


-


Cons:


Each seat only gets 1 million characters, the same as Personal. Volume per person stays flat no matter how many seats you add, so a single power user is often better off on Pro.


💡


Tip:


Numerous.ai also lets you cancel anytime and keep any tokens you've already paid for, which is a fairer setup than the "use it or lose it" credits some tools run.


## Does Numerous.ai have a free plan?


No, Numerous.ai doesn't have a permanent free plan


, but there are two ways to try it without paying much.


Every user gets


60 free tokens


(roughly 30,000 characters of input and output) when they install the add-on, according to the


[Microsoft AppSource listing](https://appsource.microsoft.com/en-us/product/office/WA200005281) . That's enough to test the


=AI()


function on a small batch of cells before you decide.


On top of that, the paid tiers come with a


7-day trial for $1


, so you can push a real workload through Pro or Enterprise for a dollar before committing to the full monthly or annual rate.


If you're mostly curious about what


=AI()


can do, the free tokens plus


[using ChatGPT inside Excel](https://julius.ai/articles/chatgpt-in-excel) will tell you fast whether the workflow fits.


## Is Numerous.ai worth it?


Numerous.ai is worth it if in-cell AI is a big part of your week,


and it's easy to skip if it isn't:


-


It's worth it if:


You run repetitive text tasks at volume, like summarizing feedback, categorizing thousands of items, or generating ad copy from a single prompt.


-


It's best for:


Marketers, researchers, and ops people who live in spreadsheets and want AI without touching code or API keys.


-


Skip it if:


You only need occasional AI help, or you need deeper analysis and charts that a cell function can't produce.


The marketplace numbers back this up. The Google Sheets add-on holds a


4.1 out of 5 across 115 ratings


with more than 502,000 users on the


[Google Workspace Marketplace](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/numerousai_chatgpt_for_sheets%EF%B8%8F/575253125118) , and the Excel version sits at


4.2 out of 5


on


[Microsoft AppSource](https://appsource.microsoft.com/en-us/product/office/WA200005281) . Those are solid scores with room to grumble.

## My bottom line on Numerous.ai pricing


I've run enough cells through Numerous.ai to say this plainly.


It does one job well


, running ChatGPT across a spreadsheet without touching an API key. It charges a fair price for that job, but it won't do much beyond it.


Your real spend comes down to the character count. A million characters sounds like a lot until you're pasting long prompts and getting paragraph-length answers back, so track a week of real use before you assume Personal covers you.


Here’s my best advice: if you buy, buy yearly


. The Personal plan alone jumps from $8 to $19 a month if you skip the annual commitment, more than double for the identical feature set.


If you need charts and dashboards, look elsewhere


. Numerous.ai keeps you inside the spreadsheet cell by cell. When you want your data pulled together into a report or a visual you can hand to someone else, a tool built for


[data analysis](https://julius.ai/articles/excel-data-analysis) will get you there faster.


For the specific job of running AI prompts across rows of data, I'd call this one of the cheaper, less complicated options on the market right now.


## Numerous.ai vs. Julius: which one fits your workflow?


Numerous.ai is built for AI inside cells you already have open. Julius starts a step earlier, since it can pull the data together before any spreadsheet exists.


Here's how to tell which one matches what you're doing:


-


Numerous.ai is better for:


Running a ChatGPT-style prompt across rows you've already built, categorizing lists, cleaning text, or generating short content cell by cell. Numerous.ai pricing at $8 a month billed annually makes this an easy call if your data already lives in a sheet and you just need AI to touch each row.


-


Julius is better for:


Starting from a question instead of a spreadsheet. Julius can search for public data or pull


[company financial data](https://julius.ai/articles/julius-ai-vs-chatgpt) on its own when you don't have a file to upload yet, then turn what it finds into charts and analysis you can act on.


-


Use both if:


You want Numerous.ai to clean and tag your raw data, then hand it to Julius to analyze and visualize. Run the row-by-row cleanup in Numerous.ai first, then pull the results into Julius for the report or dashboard you'll actually present.

## Frequently asked questions


### Is Numerous.ai free?


No, Numerous.ai isn’t free, but every user gets


60 free tokens


(about 30,000 characters) when they install the


[Numerous.ai Excel add-on](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/office/WA200005281) , plus a


7-day $1 trial on paid plans


. That's enough to test the =AI() function before you pay.


### How much does Numerous.ai cost?


Numerous.ai costs


$8 per month for Personal and $24 per month for Pro on yearly billing


, with Enterprise at $8 per user per month on a 3-seat minimum. Month-to-month billing is available at a higher rate.


### Is Numerous.ai worth it?


Yes, Numerous.ai is worth it


if you run repetitive in-cell AI tasks at volume


, like categorizing or summarizing across many rows. It's less worth it for occasional use or for real data analysis and charting.


### What is the =AI function in Numerous.ai?


The


=AI()


function


sends a prompt to ChatGPT straight from a spreadsheet cell


, then you drag it down to run the same prompt across hundreds of rows. In Excel, the equivalent function is


=NUM.AI


.


### Does Numerous.ai work in Excel and Google Sheets?


Yes, Numerous.ai works in both Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel on every plan


. Google Sheets uses the


=AI()


function, while Excel uses


=NUM.AI


.
